deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a pencil draft, with many cancellations, of the 'Lehrsätze aus der analysis situs' that open Riemann's 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (Crelle 54, 1857). The previous page drafts the introduction (Dirichlet principle, real part of w=u+vi harmonic). The next page drafts the multi-sheeted surface spread over the plane and Green/Stokes-type integration. Sketches at the top of this page show ovals and concentric circles, i.e. annuli and multiply connected regions.

(0) Top lines, very faint: a closed (unbounded) surface is to be treated as a bounded one. In the printed paper this is done by puncturing it at a point. The surface is then called n-fold connected.

(1) Definition. Suppose n closed curves a_1,...,a_n can be drawn in a surface F such that:
- no one of them, and no subset of them, completely bounds a part of F;
- but together with every other closed curve c they form the complete boundary of a part of F.
Then F is called (n+1)-fold connected.
In modern terms, {a_i} is a basis of the 1-cycles modulo bounding cycles (coefficients effectively Z/2), and the connectivity is rank H_1 + 1.

(2) Claim: the 'character' (the number n) does not depend on the choice of the system a_1..a_n.
Let b_1..b_n be another such system. By the defining property of the a's, b_1 together with some of the a's bounds a part of F. Since b_1 does not bound alone, at least one a_j occurs. Hence that a_j can be replaced by b_1 together with the remaining a's.
So b_1 plus these n-1 curves a, together with any further curve, in particular b_2, bound a part of F. Thus one of the n-1 remaining a's can be replaced by b_1, b_2 and the other n-2 a's. Repeating the procedure replaces all a's by b's.
The fragmentary sentence 'dass die Curven b zur vollständigen Begrenzung ... nicht hinreichen, so lange ...' says the b's do not suffice for bounding until all a's have been replaced. This is the Steinitz-type exchange argument for the invariance of the dimension of a basis.

(3) A remark that, if the boundary can be cut through the interior everywhere, the surface can be turned into a simply connected one.

(4) Theorem: an (n+1)-fold connected surface F can be changed into an n-fold connected surface by a cross-cut (Querschnitt). A cross-cut is a line running through the interior from one boundary point to a boundary point. The trailing fragment 'die die Curven a_1,...,a_n ... So muss ... durchschneidet' starts the proof: the cut must cross the curves a_i.

Nothing is computed. The page sets up the topological apparatus (connectivity order, cross-cuts) needed to make the Abelian integrals single-valued on the cut surface T'.
errors: The exchange step tacitly assumes the new system (b_1, a_2..a_n) again has the defining property: no subset bounds. This holds working modulo 2 (or with integer multiplicities), but Riemann does not check it. Riemann's 'bounding' notion is never made precise as to orientation and multiplicity. Later critics (Tonelli 1875, and the Betti/Poincaré refinements) pointed this out.

The argument as drafted only shows the b's can replace the a's one by one. To conclude the two systems have equal cardinality, one also needs that a system of fewer than n curves cannot have the full property, or must run the exchange symmetrically. Here this is left implicit.

The cross-cut theorem is stated but its proof breaks off. In general it requires that the cut not separate the surface; a separating cut gives two pieces. The printed version handles this case separately.

results.what: Definition of the order of connectivity ((n+1)-fold connected) via a maximal system of n closed curves that do not jointly bound but bound together with any further closed curve
results.modern_name: connectivity number = first Betti number (mod 2) + 1; basis of H_1(F; Z/2)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1851/1857 (Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen); formalized by Betti 1871 and Poincaré 1895

results.what: Invariance of the number n under change of curve system, by successive exchange of a-curves for b-curves
results.modern_name: exchange lemma (Steinitz exchange) giving invariance of homology rank
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1857 for this topological use; the linear-algebra exchange lemma to Grassmann/Steinitz (1913)

results.what: A cross-cut (boundary point to boundary point through the interior) reduces an (n+1)-fold connected surface to an n-fold connected one
results.modern_name: cutting a surface along a non-separating arc lowers the first Betti number by one (Euler characteristic increases by 1)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of the published analysis-situs section of Riemann's 1857 Abelian functions paper; the definitions and the exchange argument appear in print. It is of interest only as evidence of the drafting process, e.g. the explicit exchange argument and the treatment of closed surfaces as bounded.

checkable.asserts: A genus-p closed orientable surface punctured once (Euler characteristic 1-2p) is (2p+1)-fold connected in Riemann's sense, i.e. connectivity = 2 - chi = rank H_1 + 1.
A non-separating cross-cut raises chi by 1 and so lowers the connectivity (2 - chi) by exactly 1, as in the Querschnitt theorem.

checkable.asserts: Toy exchange: replacing a_1 by b_1=a_1+a_2 keeps a basis of rank 2 in a 2-dimensional homology (annulus with hole, or torus-type example), illustrating invariance of n.

transcription_corrections: Line beginning 'Wenn sich in einer Fläche F n ... geschlossene Curven a_1, a_2, ..., a_n ziehen lassen': the image reads approximately 'welche für sich und miteinander keinen Theil dieser Fläche F vollständig begrenzen, mit jeder andern geschlossenen Curve aber die vollständige Begrenzung eines Theils der Fläche bilden'. The negation 'nicht/keinen' belongs to the first clause.
The connectivity phrase reads 'So heisst die Fläche eine n+1 fach zusammenhängende' (pencil insertion above, with 'n+1' clearly visible).
'Der Charakter der Fläche ist unabhängig von der Wahl des Curvensystems' is correct.
The two faint lines near the top right appear to be 'n fach zusammenhängend' / 'zusammenhängend'. They label the figures: ovals with holes and concentric circles (annuli).
The lower fragment 'dass die Curven b zur vollständigen Begrenzung eines Theils von F nicht hinreichen ...' is uncertain; it may read 'ersieht man ... dass die Curven b ... ausreichen'.
